explanation: The two-job execution is faulty because the highest-demand qualifying record n06-r01 was omitted before the downstream handoff. Job 2 consumed exact controller-recorded handoffs and processed the seven records it received, but the upstream normalize function filtered selected records through an allowed_record_ids list that excludes n06-r01 and includes n06-r09 instead. That caused the needs and evidence_sources handoffs to lack n06-r01, violating the requirement to select and retain all qualifying or fallback demand records while preserving identities and provenance.
cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus includes record_id n06-r01 with demand_score 9, so it qualifies under the visible select_demand threshold demand_score >= 3.
select_demand selected_df has 8 rows and selected output state has 8 rows, showing n06-r01 was initially retained by job_1.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids = ['n06-r09', 'n06-r02', 'n06-r03', 'n06-r04', 'n06-r05', 'n06-r06', 'n06-r07', 'n06-r08'], excluding n06-r01.
normalize retained_df and final needs_df states have 7 rows, matching the downstream input needs of only n06-r02 through n06-r08.
handoff-needs and handoff-evidence-sources have matching producer and consumer hashes, so Job 2 consumed the exact upstream artifacts rather than dropping n06-r01 itself.
